answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie earning power to a slow-maturing work history rather than to account creation: each identity builds a cipher-signed record of completed, peer-verified tasks, and only that record unlocks higher reward tiers. Like a zephyr that cannot be bottled on demand, trust gathers gradually over a long horizon, so spawning a thousand empty identities buys nothing, while one agent doing real, checkable work steadily gains weight.
